concept.name: Oracle
concept.definition: A blockchain oracle is a service that sources, verifies and transmits off-chain data (prices, events, computation results) onto the blockchain so that smart contracts — which cannot access external data themselves — can act on it.
concept.intuition: Contracts are sealed in a deterministic box and can't browse the internet; the oracle is the courier that slips verified notes under the door.
concept.mechanics: An on-chain oracle contract receives data requests; off-chain oracle nodes query APIs or data sources, reach agreement (e.g. via median aggregation across many nodes, as in Chainlink price feeds), and post the result on-chain where any contract can read it. Decentralized oracle networks use multiple independent nodes and sources plus staking/reputation to resist manipulation.
concept.failure_modes: If the oracle reports a wrong or stale price, lending protocols liquidate solvent users or let attackers drain pools with mispriced collateral; single-source or centralized oracles are one hack or outage away from corrupting every dependent contract ('the oracle problem').
concept.misconceptions: Oracles do not make off-chain data trustless — they shift trust to the oracle network's aggregation and incentives. A decentralized oracle with many nodes but one upstream data source still has a single point of failure.
concept.example: Aave reads a Chainlink ETH/USD price feed to value collateral; if the feed briefly reported ETH at half its true price, thousands of loans would instantly fall below their liquidation thresholds through no fault of borrowers.
